Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B0. The Academy attests لاذَ, لَوْذًا/لِياذًا/لِواذًا, أَلاذَ, لاوَذَ, المَلاذ and related nouns.
The second radical is و. The Qur’anic لِوَاذًا is a Form-III verbal noun in the refuge/avoidance branch; ordinary hollow-vowel alternation is not counted as a separate form.
لَوْذٌ and لِيَاذٌ were considered as genuine maṣdar variants, but are lexical variants of the same refuge action rather than better additional morphology.
لِوَاذًا without its case ending was not counted separately.
Article, preposition and any attached material were not counted.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B4. The Academy attests ناشَ, ناوَشَ, تَناوَشَ and اِنْتاشَ in movement, reaching, taking and engagement branches.
The second radical is و. The Qur’anic Form-VI verbal noun is retained as the current form; hollow contraction and inflection are not separate rows.
تَنَاوَشَ and تَنَاوُشٌ are the verbal form and maṣdar represented by the current Qur’anic family; the current form itself already supplies that row.
نَوْشٌ was considered as a maṣdar but was not added alongside the current Form-VI maṣdar to avoid near-duplicate verbal-noun rows.
The definite article and nominative ending in ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ were not counted separately.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%86%D9%88%D8%B5. The Academy attests ناصَ, نَوْصًا/نَوَصانًا, أَناصَ, ناوَصَ, اِنْتاصَ, اسْتَناصَ and المَناصُ as refuge, movement, escape and seeking branches.
The second radical is و. مَنَاصٌ is a place noun meaning refuge or escape; its lexical family is broader than the surface noun but must remain within root ن و ص.
أَنَاصَ was considered, but the selected basic verb, imperfect, maṣdar and Form-X pattern give a clearer teaching progression.
مَنَاصٌ without its case ending was not counted separately.
The meaning of مَنَاصٌ was not flattened into the verb’s full semantic range; it remains refuge/escape.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D8%B2%D9%88%D9%84. The Academy attests زالَ, زَوَالًا, أَزالَ, زاوَلَ, زَوَّلَ, انْزالَ, الزّائِلُ and related forms.
The second radical is و. زَوَالٌ is the maṣdar/noun of cessation, departure or disappearance; the same root also has a causative removal branch.
زَوْلٌ and زَوَّلَ were considered; زَوْلٌ belongs to a distinct lively/clever noun branch, while زَوَّلَ would add less value than the selected basic/causative contrast.
The earlier C1 family using لِتَزُولَ is a separate Qur’anic occurrence family; this family is adjudicated independently with the same canonical root.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D8%A8%D9%88%D8%B1. The Academy attests بارَ, بَوْرًا/بَوارًا, أَبارَ, بَوَّرَ, ابْتارَ, بائِرٌ, بُورٌ and البَوارُ.
The second radical is و. البَوارُ is the destruction/ruin noun; the root also includes perishing, failure, barrenness and causing ruin.
بَوْرٌ and بُورٌ were considered as genuine noun variants, but the selected verb, imperfect, participle and causative give stronger morphology.
The article in ٱلْبَوَارِ and its genitive ending were not counted separately.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%82%D9%88%D8%AA. The Academy attests قاتَ, أَقاتَ, اقْتاتَ, تَقَوَّتَ, اسْتَقاتَ, القُوتُ and المُقِيتُ.
The second radical is و. The Qur’anic مُقِيتٌ is an active participle in the Form-IV sustaining/providing branch, not the noun قُوتٌ itself.
تَقَوَّتَ and اسْتَقاتَ were investigated but were not needed after selecting the basic verb, Form-IV, Form-VIII and root noun.
The doubled consonant in مُقِيتًا is not a new root; it is the established Form-IV participial pattern.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D8%AE%D9%8A%D8%B7. The Academy attests خاطَ, خَيِطَ, خَيَّطَ, اخْتاطَ, تَخَيَّطَ, الخِياطُ, الخِياطةُ, الخَيْطُ, الخَيّاطُ, المَخِيطُ and المِخْيَطُ.
The second radical is ي. The Qur’anic الخِياطِ is the needle/instrument noun; the family also contains sewing verbs, the craft noun and the tailor noun.
مِخْيَطٌ was investigated and is genuine for needle, but it substantially repeats the current instrument meaning الخِياطِ; مَخِيطٌ gives better morphological diversity.
خَيْطٌ itself is the material noun ‘thread’ and was considered, but the selected set more directly explains the Qur’anic needle/craft branch.
The long vowel in الخِياطِ is lexical patterning, not evidence for a different root.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.
Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D8%B2%D9%88%D8%AF. The Academy attests زادَ, أَزادَ, زوَّدَ, تَزَوَّدَ, الزّادُ and المِزْوَدُ.
The second radical is و. The Qur’anic الزَّادِ is the provision noun; the root has basic preparation, giving, supplying and taking-provision branches.
المِزْوَدُ was considered as a place/container noun, but the selected verb-pattern progression teaches more about the Qur’anic provision word.
The article and genitive ending in ٱلزَّادِ were not counted.
The current form plus four independently attested same-root forms provide useful lexical and morphological development without shell, case, pronoun or contraction padding.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%87%D9%88%D8%B1. The Academy attests هارَ, هَوْرًا/هُؤُورًا, هَوَّرَ, اهْتَوَرَ, انْهارَ, الهائِرُ and الهارُ.
The second radical is و. The Qur’anic هَارٍ is a lexical adjective describing something collapsing or eroding; it is not merely a surface contraction of an ordinary verb form.
هَائِرٌ and الهَارُ were considered as genuine adjective/agent branches, but the selected maṣdar and derived verbs provide more useful morphology around the Qur’anic form.
The Qur’anic tanwīn and genitive ending in هَارٍ were not counted separately.
